## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to normalize heterogeneous log formats into a single, streamable standard while handling compression and rotations. It also probes deduplication, timestamp normalization, and ordering under real-world constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Robust format detection (plain vs JSON)
- On-the-fly decompressing of gzip logs
- Timestamp normalization to a common ISO8601
- Time-window filtering (last 60 minutes)
- Deduplication across rotated files

## Code Example

```bash
# Example approach (not executable as-is):
for f in /logs/app-logs/*/log-*.log /logs/app-logs/*/log-*.log.gz; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  case "$f" in
    *.gz) zcat "$f" ;; *) cat "$f" ;; esac
  fi
done | \
awk 'BEGIN{now=systime(); win=3600}# ...
''
```

- How to integrate with a central sink (e.g., Kafka) while preserving order?

questions.explanation:
## Identifying D-State Processes

- Use `ps` with state filtering to find uninterruptible processes
- Check system logs for hardware or filesystem errors
- Examine I/O queues and block device status

## Common Causes

- NFS mount issues or network storage problems
- Faulty hardware devices (disk, controller)
- Kernel bugs or driver issues
- Memory pressure causing I/O blocking

## Resolution Strategies

- Wait for hardware timeout (usually 30-120 seconds)
- Check and fix underlying storage issues
- Reboot as last resort if process won't recover
- Monitor `/proc/<PID>/stack` for kernel call traces

```bash
for fd in /proc/*/fd/*; do

    tgt=$(readlink "$fd" 2>/dev/null)

  fi
```
